contract: A tool written in Lua as one pure pattern step over PatternStep v1 neutral maps: for the start input it asks for one local-work run action that replays the function from the start with the record of earlier module calls as a sandbox request (calls mode replay), and ends with the final value or with the first module call that has no record; for such a call it checks the name and index against the record and the bindings, the call limit and the arguments (LuaBinding.check_arguments/3), asks for one tool-call action, checks the result (LuaBinding.check_result/3), adds the call to the record and asks for the run again; one finish, completed with the value and the identity of the run action, or failed with a named reason. One action in each request; no action is asked for twice and no outcome starts a second try. State within 65,536 bytes. It runs no Lua and calls no module; no sandbox state is kept, only the record.
limits: The step runs no Lua and calls no module: each test input is a literal neutral map, no sandbox is run and the Piece does not depend on runtime/lua-sandbox; the form of the run payload and of the four run-result forms is shown against literal forms of the sandbox, not against its code.

No ready parent reads elzoo.lua-tool.result: the host wraps the step in a function of its own that turns the finish into the form of the parent; a Run in which another pattern also makes tool calls gives the engine a schema map for the tool_call kind, with an entry for elzoo.lua-tool.module-call; with one binding for the kind, the module results arrive under the other pattern's result schema and each module call ends as module_call_not_completed.

A run or a module call that did not complete ends the tool as failed and is never repeated; a replay whose call order differs from the record is a failure, never a repair; each module call costs one more sandbox run from the start, so a tool with n calls runs n + 1 times; a memory or wall-time stop is a host outcome and ends the tool as failed.
No Cure law is selected: the decisions of the step table have finite recorded-trace tests only; no universal claim.

grounding.claim: Nine named recorded-trace groups pass: no_module_call, two_module_calls_in_order, restart_between_calls, call_order_differs, undeclared_and_wrong_arguments, sandbox_stops_are_tool_failures, module_call_not_completed, limits_and_closed and forms_agree; plus the checked example of one module call. Each request passes PatternStep.decode/1. Negative controls: skipping the index test of a pending call fails call_order_differs; starting a second run after a failed run fails sandbox_stops_are_tool_failures. state_is_plain_data: the state is plain data (no struct) within 65,536 bytes after every transition of the trace of two_module_calls_in_order, by the measure of the ready run engine. Finite scenarios, not a universal proof.

Pinned Elixir immutable maps and lists; the ready Contracts of workflow/pattern-step, workflow/tool-registry and runtime/lua-binding are reused unchanged; the state bound is measured as the byte size of :erlang.term_to_binary(state, [:deterministic, {:minor_version, 2}]), the measure of the ready run engine.

The host supplies an engine that records each input before the step reads it and checks payload, budget, authority and approval for every action; a local_work binding that runs exactly the given request with the sandbox on an executable that the host built and returns the run-result form; a tool_call binding for each alias of the binding source that calls the real Adapter of the module and returns the module-result form; a recipe whose functions and permissions passed workflow/recipe-check; a Run-wide unique id; and results small enough for the state bound.

telemetry.contract: Pure step emits no observations; the engine owns instrumentation.

config.contract: Intrinsic spec operands and fixed bounds (state 65,536 bytes, 256 module calls); no ambient or hot settings.

control.contract: No independent process; cancel and run_ended are pattern inputs, not operational commands.
